subject: Science
title: Year 7 Science: Half-term 2 (Particles, states of matter and mixtures)

questions.question: Which statement about liquids is true?
options: They take the shape of their container
questions.answer: They take the shape of their container
questions.explanation: Liquid particles touch but can slide past each other, so liquids flow and take their container's shape.

questions.question: What is the change from gas to liquid called?
questions.explanation: Gas to liquid is condensing, e.g. water droplets forming on a cold window.

questions.question: Ice melts at 0°C. What happens to the particles as the ice melts?
options: They gain energy and break out of their fixed positions
questions.answer: They gain energy and break out of their fixed positions
questions.explanation: Heat gives the particles energy; they break free of the fixed pattern and can move past each other.

questions.question: What is the difference between evaporation and boiling?
options: Evaporation happens only at the surface, at any temperature below boiling point
Boiling happens only at the surface
questions.answer: Evaporation happens only at the surface, at any temperature below boiling point
questions.explanation: Evaporation happens at the surface at any temperature; boiling happens throughout the liquid at its boiling point.

questions.question: Why does the smell of perfume spread across a room?
options: The perfume particles move randomly and spread out
questions.answer: The perfume particles move randomly and spread out
questions.explanation: Gas particles move quickly and randomly, so they diffuse through the air.

questions.question: Why does a balloon get bigger when it is warmed?
options: The gas particles move faster and hit the walls harder
questions.answer: The gas particles move faster and hit the walls harder
questions.explanation: Faster particles collide with the walls more often and harder, increasing pressure inside.

questions.question: Which of these is a pure substance?
questions.explanation: Distilled water contains only water particles. The others are mixtures.

questions.question: Sugar dissolves in tea. In this solution, what is the solute?
questions.explanation: The solute is what dissolves (sugar); the solvent is what it dissolves in (the liquid).

questions.question: Which method separates the different dyes in a black ink?
questions.explanation: Chromatography separates dyes because they travel different distances up the paper.

questions.question: Which method gets pure water from sea water?
questions.explanation: Distillation boils the water and condenses the vapour, leaving the salt behind.

questions.question: Iron filings are mixed with sand. What is the easiest way to separate them?
questions.explanation: Iron is magnetic and sand is not.

questions.question: Why does more sugar dissolve in hot water than in cold water?
questions.explanation: Most solids are more soluble at higher temperatures.
